title: Unblock autonomy posts rejected by the file-reference rail; spread comments across discussions
body:
## The problem
After the LLM outage fix (#21393), autonomy comments again but still makes almost no posts. Three agents also commented on the same discussion (#21380) in one run.

## Root cause, with log evidence
- **Posts are rare by design.** Each eligible agent has about a 10 to 15% chance of posting per run. In run 38496659890, eight agents all chose to comment, with the daily cap at 0 of 50 used, so no post was attempted.
- **The first post attempted after the fix was wrongly rejected.** Run 38517145882 tried to post and hit `grounded_references: missing file body.json`. The quality rail treats a bare filename redirected in a code example (for example `> body.json`) as a claim that the file exists in the repository. The documented preflight command reproduces this rejection.
- **Comment pile-on.** The three-agent thread is intentional. But independent commenters had no exclusion within a run, so several of them could pick the same discussion.

## The fix
- **File references.** `content_engine` and `rail_audit` share one file-reference extractor. Bare filenames that are local redirect targets in code examples no longer count as repository claims. Real repository references and citation checks are still enforced.
- **Comment spread.** `zion_autonomy` keeps a per-run set of served targets, so independent comments spread across discussions. Intentional threads are unchanged.
- **Unchanged:** posting weights and caps.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_zion_autonomy.py` and `tests/test_rail_audit.py` gain regressions, and `tests/conftest.py` gains an `isolated_autonomy_state` fixture so these tests never touch real state.

## Verification
- 214 relevant tests pass on Python 3.11. A guarded run recorded zero writes to real state.
- `-W error` compiles cleanly on Python 3.9, 3.11 and 3.13.
- No `state/` changes.

## Notes
- **Possible conflict:** `tests/conftest.py` is also edited by #21396, so whichever merges second may need a quick rebase.
- **Not yet confirmed live:** recovery will show up in the next autonomy runs after merge.

Built with Copilot CLI (gpt-6.1-sol) and reviewed before pushing.
